label: Unit 2
theme: If This, Then That—Do It Again
intro: Keep the floor robot and give it one rule. He has to notice the cue before he moves. Repeats belong in the room with you; the bee grid still runs direction arrows.

gelds.text: Choosing an action from a visible cue
Repeating a short unit without changing its order
Finding and replacing one wrong step

tryNote: Use two colored cards and enough clear floor for five steps. One rule at a time.

daily.title: Show the other card
daily.do: Say, "If I show green, clap." Show green and let him clap. The card has to do the prompting.
daily.stretch: Add, "If I show red, hands in lap." Switch cards and ask which cue made him choose that action.

daily.title: Clap, then tap
daily.do: Clap, then tap your knees. He copies the pair once. Keep the two actions separate.
daily.stretch: He names the repeating pair and does it three times in the same order, counting each pair on his fingers afterward.

daily.title: Fix just the bug
daily.do: Plan a three-step route to a cushion and say the directions before walking it. Put one wrong arrow down for him to find.
daily.stretch: Make a four- or five-move route, then replace only the wrong arrow and run it again. Starting over hides which step failed.

goalsTitle: What he should have by the end of this unit

his: Plans and says a four- or five-move route using up, down, left, and right before pressing Run.
Follows a spoken if/then rule and explains which visible cue made him act.
Chooses the other action when the cue changes in a two-choice rule.
Spots a two-action repeating unit and performs it three times without changing its order.
Calls a wrong step a bug, identifies it, and corrects that step in a spoken routine without rebuilding the whole routine.

weekend: Let him write the family robot rule with two picture cards. You follow it literally, including the mistake, and let him change the instruction.

songs.title: If I See It
songs.style: Start singing immediately, with no instrumental intro. Light woodblocks and hand claps with clear gaps for copying each action. One clear warm voice, short repeated melody, steady preschool pace, clean ending without a long outro.
lyrics: If it's green, then clap, clap, clap.
If it's red, put hands in lap.
Clap, then tap; clap, then tap.
Clap, then tap; clap, then tap.

basic.label: Red circle
basic.note: A red circle can be the cue for hands in your lap.

basic.label: Green circle
basic.note: A green circle can be the cue for a clap.

advanced.label: Blue square
advanced.note: A square has four straight sides.

advanced.label: Purple square
advanced.note: Look for both purple and square.

advanced.label: Orange diamond
advanced.note: This orange diamond has four corners.

advanced.label: Star
advanced.note: A star can be a cue when a person gives it a rule.

advanced.label: Heart
advanced.note: The heart picture can be a cue to tap your chest.

advanced.label: Repeat arrow
advanced.note: The repeat arrow says to do the same part again.

lines.start: Tell the bee how to get to the flower.
lines.wall: The bee bumped into something. Fix your program and try again.
lines.stop: The bee stopped in the wrong place. Fix your program and try again.

sort.title: Did It Follow the Rule?
sort.sub: Follows the rule or Different action

items.text: The rule is green means clap; you see green and clap.
items.note: The green cue called for a clap.

items.text: The rule is red means sit; you see red and jump.
The rule is up arrow means hands up; you see up and raise your hands.
The rule is down arrow means crouch; you see down and stand tall.
items.note: The down arrow called for crouching.

items.text: The rule is star means tap; you see a star and tap.
items.note: The star cue called for a tap.

items.text: The rule is heart means wave; you see a heart and clap.
items.note: A wave was the heart rule.

items.text: The rule is blue means step left; you see blue and step left.
items.note: You chose the step named in the rule.

items.text: The rule is yellow means stop; you see yellow and keep walking.
items.note: Stop means leave your feet still.

items.text: The rule is triangle means turn; you see a triangle and turn.
items.note: The cue and the action match the rule.

items.text: Green means clap and red means sit; the card changes to red and you clap.
items.note: The new red cue calls for the other action.

items.text: Blue means left and yellow means right; the card changes to yellow and you step right.
items.note: You changed your action when the cue changed.

items.text: The rule is clap then tap, twice; you clap, tap, clap, tap.
items.note: The same two-action part happened twice.

items.text: The rule is clap then tap, twice; you clap, clap, tap, tap.
items.note: The actions are there, but the repeated part changed order.

items.text: Up means hands high and down means hands low; you see down but copy Dad raising his hands.
items.note: The arrow was the cue, even when Dad did something else.

steps.text: Pick the flower as the goal
Place up as the first move
Say red means hands in lap
Choose clap as the first action
Choose knee tap as the second
Put the two action cards in that order
Say green means clap and red means sit
